mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with broader economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp does not correlate with increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals increased economic activity and supply-side growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% signals a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to decreased investment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 4% does not correlate with decreased investment.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals strong job growth, which is a leading indicator for consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong consumer-driven economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with a strong consumer-driven economy.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% over the previous 3 months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to increased investment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during periods of economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.25% does not correlate with increased investment during periods of economic uncertainty.
